title: plugin-approvals: the schema-read participant probe scans sys_approval_action unindexed on every hidden-object list read
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cwJbS8sZAfru2iyvQq

Filing gate: ② performance, class b. Found by the contract review of PR #32998 (record 6844571138, nit N1), and read from the code on `main` after `8004529e51`. ⛔ Not a claim.
reach: any object list read (`GET /api/v1/meta/object`, the dispatcher, HTTP and stdio MCP) by a caller who cannot read `sys_approval_request` / `sys_approval_action`, and any other outlet that asks the object-schema posture about those two objects.

## What happens

Since #32955 (PR #32998), the schema-read posture asks the declared `schemaReadDelegate` service, which is plugin-approvals' `authorizeSchemaRead`, whenever `canReadObject` refuses one of the two objects. To answer yes or no, the service runs the participant probe it uses for its own door: up to five reads. One of them is a scan of `sys_approval_action` on `actor_id` / `acted_as`, neither of which is indexed. It collects up to three 10 000-row windows and sends them back as one `$in`. Before #32998, only the approvals door's own reads paid this cost. Now every hidden-object list read by such a caller does. Results are memoized per request context only.

## Expected

The existence question is answered with a bounded probe (limit 1, or an `exists`-shaped read) instead of collecting id windows, and `sys_approval_action` carries an index on the participant columns the probe filters on. Both belong in one card, so the probe and its index land together.

## Business reason

In an organization with a long approval history, every metadata list read by an ordinary member, such as opening the app or loading an object picker, pays for a scan of the whole approval action log. That cost grows with the log, and no request ever needs more than a yes or no.

Correctness and the contract are unaffected. The answer is right today, only expensive.

Dedupe words: `authorizeSchemaRead probe cost`, `sys_approval_action index actor_id`, `schemaReadDelegate participant probe`.
Related: #32955 (PR #32998), ADR-0106.
